product.lead: Clamp-on sensors, our own machine learning models and a digital twin of your plumbing. Installed in seconds, scaled across your whole portfolio.

visual.alt: Diagram: a clamp-on sensor on a pipe sends readings into a live-flow chart with its learned baseline, a deviation is placed on the building's digital twin and raised as an alert.

install.h2: What does an install look like?
install.text: Our proprietary sensors clamp onto existing pipes in 30 seconds each, with no pipe cutting and no shutdown. Your own team can install them.
install.visualAlt: Diagram: clamp-on ultrasonic flow sensors on a riser and on the supply line that feeds it.

data.text: One dashboard with live flow per measuring point and every alert ranked by severity. Each alert names the building, the riser and what to check first.
data.visualAlt: Sample chart: one measuring point over seven days, the learned baseline band and a deviation on the last two days.

chart.title: Measuring point, riser B, seven days

precision.text: To the riser or the building section. The search starts at the right floors, not behind the first wet wall.

ml.text: Our proprietary machine learning, built for hydraulic systems, learns each building's normal flow and flags what normal does not explain. Your team's feedback makes it sharper with every building.
ml.visualAlt: Measuring points, each with its learned baseline band and live flow. One riser departs from its baseline and is flagged.

sensors.intro: Proprietary clamp-on sensors on existing pipework. Nothing is cut.

visual.alt: Digital twin of a clamp-on ultrasonic flow sensor: two transducers strapped to the outside of a pipe, the ultrasonic path through the water, and the flow direction.

twin.text: A model of the building's plumbing that turns a deviation into a place to check first.

faq.q: Does the install interrupt the water supply?
faq.a: No. Sensors clamp onto the outside of the pipe and the water stays on.

faq.q: How long does a rollout take?
faq.a: Fast, and it scales. Each sensor clamps on in 30 seconds, so your own team can bring many buildings live in parallel.

faq.q: Does it work with old pipes?
faq.a: Yes. The sensors clamp onto any accessible pipe, old or new.
Alerts are ranked by severity and reviewed with your team. Your feedback makes the models sharper with every building.
You and the people you name. We do not sell data, see the privacy policy.
Priced per building and measuring point, a fraction of one claim. We quote from your plumbing plan.

steps.name: Map
steps.text: Send us the plumbing plan or walk us through once. We place the sensors and build the digital twin.

steps.name: Install
steps.text: 30 seconds per sensor. No pipe cutting, the water stays on.

steps.name: Learn
steps.text: Our model learns the building's normal flow.

steps.name: Detect
steps.text: Deviations are ranked by severity and localized to the riser. Your team gets the place to check first.

faq.q: We have smart water meters. Is this the same?
faq.a: No. Meters count use per unit, while AquaShield learns normal flow at the riser and catches leaks no single meter sees.

faq.q: Do we need to open walls?
faq.a: No. Sensors clamp onto accessible pipe in risers, basements and shafts.

faq.q: What does our maintenance team have to do?
faq.a: Clamp on the sensors, or let us do it. Then act on the alerts: each one names the riser and the floors to check first.

faq.q: Does it work in old buildings?
faq.a: Yes. The sensors clamp onto any accessible pipe, old or new.
One. Roll out when you have seen it work.

faq.q: Can our insurer see the data?
faq.a: Only if you decide so. Some portfolios share it to negotiate better terms.

insurance.h1: Shorter loss duration. Lower claim severity.
insurance.lead: For property underwriters, claims and innovation leads.

story.lead: A hidden leak runs until someone notices. Every extra day adds secondary damage: subfloors, drywall, neighboring units, business interruption.

timeline.alt: Timeline. Without monitoring, a hidden leak runs for weeks. It reaches the subfloor, the drywall, the neighboring unit and business interruption before a tenant discovers it. With AquaShield, a flow deviation is flagged early, the riser is located and the rest of the loss is avoided.

levers.name: Lever 1: shorter loss duration
levers.text: Earlier detection shortens the loss. Fewer days of water means less secondary damage and a smaller claim.

levers.name: Lever 2: a live risk signal
levers.text: Flow data per riser is a risk signal that underwriting does not have today, from buildings that are already instrumented.

story.h2: Floor leak cables tell you after the fact.

how.h2: How it works on a cooling loop.

steps.name: Clamp on
steps.text: Ultrasonic flow sensors clamp onto every rack branch. No cutting into the cooling loop, no downtime.

steps.name: Learn the loop
steps.text: The model learns the normal flow of every branch and how the branches move together.

steps.name: Flag the branch
steps.text: One branch drifts from its neighbors. The alert names the rack before water reaches the floor.

chapters.title: The hackathon
chapters.text: Paul and Marguerite meet at an MIT hackathon and win it with AquaShield. The week after, they clamp the first sensors onto pipes in a campus building.
chapters.alt: Paul Beckers and Marguerite Benoist in front of the Great Dome at MIT.

chapters.title: Y Combinator
chapters.text: Spring 2026, months of building at full speed among people doing the same. That pace never left us, and part of us still lives in San Francisco.
chapters.alt: Marguerite Benoist and Paul Beckers behind the Y Combinator sign in San Francisco.

chapters.title: The team
chapters.text: Today we build from Zurich, one of Europe's strongest hubs for robotics and machine learning. Our models get sharper with every building, and the team grows with people who want to build them.
chapters.alt: The AquaShield team around a table of laptops in the Zurich office.

items.name: Driven
items.text: We move at a pace most teams find unreasonable. We like it that way.

items.name: Think big, ship fast
items.text: US mentality in a European team. Decide today, ship this week, sell before it is perfect.

items.name: Loyal
items.text: We back each other. On site, in the lab and when it gets hard.

items.name: Smart and efficient
items.text: The best idea wins, whoever it comes from. Then we take the shortest path to it.

items.name: Open and transparent
items.text: Problems go on the table early. Feedback is direct and goes both ways.

items.name: Out of the lab
items.text: We deploy early, in real basements and plant rooms, next to the people who run the building.

items.name: Hardware in the field
